question.:question/problem:
Consider the differential equation

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\sec{\left(\frac{3 x}{y} \right)}.
$$

If the transformation $y=v(x)x$ is applied to the differential equation, what is the resulting equation?
question.:question/worked-solution:
Using the transformation $y=vx$ (where $v=v(x)$), we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}+v\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(x) \\  & =x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}+v.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the above into the given differential equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\sec{\left(\frac{3 x}{y} \right)} \\ x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}+v & =\sec{\left(\frac{3}{v} \right)} \\ x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}+v & =\sec{\left(\frac{3}{v} \right)} \\ x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x} & =- v + \sec{\left(\frac{3}{v} \right)} \\ x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x} & =- v + \sec{\left(\frac{3}{v} \right)} \\ \left(- \frac{1}{v - \sec{\left(\frac{3}{v} \right)}}\right)\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{1}{x}.\end{aligned}
$$

Consider the differential equation

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=- 4 \sin{\left(\frac{y}{x} \right)} + \frac{3 y}{x}.
$$

If the transformation $y=v(x)x$ is applied to the differential equation, what is the resulting equation?
question.:question/worked-solution:
Using the transformation $y=vx$ (where $v=v(x)$), we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}+v\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(x) \\  & =x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}+v.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the above into the given differential equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =- 4 \sin{\left(\frac{y}{x} \right)} + \frac{3 y}{x} \\ x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}+v & =3 v - 4 \sin{\left(v \right)} \\ x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}+v & =3 v - 4 \sin{\left(v \right)} \\ x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x} & =2 v - 4 \sin{\left(v \right)} \\ x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x} & =2 v - 4 \sin{\left(v \right)} \\ \left(\frac{1}{2 v - 4 \sin{\left(v \right)}}\right)\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{1}{x}.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
Consider the differential equation

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\frac{3 x^{2} - x y + y^{2}}{x^{2} + y^{2}}.
$$

If the transformation $y=v(x)x$ is applied to the differential equation, what is the resulting equation?
question.:question/worked-solution:
Using the transformation $y=vx$ (where $v=v(x)$), we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}+v\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(x) \\  & =x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}+v.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the above into the given differential equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{3 x^{2} - x y + y^{2}}{x^{2} + y^{2}} \\ x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}+v & =\frac{v^{2} x^{2} - v x^{2} + 3 x^{2}}{v^{2} x^{2} + x^{2}} \\ x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}+v & =\frac{v^{2} - v + 3}{v^{2} + 1} \\ x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x} & =- v + \frac{v^{2} - v + 3}{v^{2} + 1} \\ x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{- v^{3} + v^{2} - 2 v + 3}{v^{2} + 1} \\ \left(\frac{- v^{2} - 1}{v^{3} - v^{2} + 2 v - 3}\right)\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{1}{x}.\end{aligned}
$$

Consider the differential equation

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=e^{\sin{\left(\frac{4 y}{x} \right)}} - \frac{2 y}{x}.
$$

If the transformation $y=v(x)x$ is applied to the differential equation, what is the resulting equation?
question.:question/worked-solution:
Using the transformation $y=vx$ (where $v=v(x)$), we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}+v\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(x) \\  & =x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}+v.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the above into the given differential equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =e^{\sin{\left(\frac{4 y}{x} \right)}} - \frac{2 y}{x} \\ x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}+v & =- 2 v + e^{\sin{\left(4 v \right)}} \\ x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}+v & =- 2 v + e^{\sin{\left(4 v \right)}} \\ x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x} & =- 3 v + e^{\sin{\left(4 v \right)}} \\ x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x} & =- 3 v + e^{\sin{\left(4 v \right)}} \\ \left(- \frac{1}{3 v - e^{\sin{\left(4 v \right)}}}\right)\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{1}{x}.\end{aligned}
$$
